nodes.label: Feature List With Phase Tags And Explicit Non-Goals
nodes.rationale: Items marked [—] are deliberate non-goals, not oversights: merge/branches/textual diff, direct-to-printer sending, geometry editing ever, catalogue scraping, full MRP, per-widget polling (a self-inflicted DoS), and phone-home licence checks.

nodes.label: Move History: Route Only, Deliberately Unread
nodes.rationale: GET /api/parts/{id}/moves shipped and answers correctly, but nothing displays it — a product call taken 2026-09-07, not an oversight: a 'moved from' line is history about a thing whose current location the card already shows. Its [] answer for an unknown part id is the same as 'never moved', deliberately, because nothing acts differently on the two.

nodes.label: Page Size And Density Per Viewer, Per Library
nodes.rationale: 'Per library' would have meant a column, but with no user table, session table or auth in Phase 1 a column makes one operator's choice everybody's — and is wrong the moment auth arrives. Stored in the browser keyed by library id: each library remembers its own setting, and the memory is that browser's.

nodes.label: Licence On The Detail Page, Not The Grid Card
nodes.rationale: Half of hobbyist STL libraries are non-commercial and somebody selling prints needs to see CC-BY-NC first, but the grid query is at its 16-column FromRow ceiling and reworking that tuple to put a sentence on a tile someone is scanning at a glance is the wrong trade. It is one click away, in the quick-look, which is where the decision to print is actually made.

nodes.label: OpenGraph Fetching Is Out
nodes.rationale: Owner decision. part_image.origin still carries og_fetched so adding it later stays additive, and DATA.md is emphatic about where that road ends.

nodes.label: Source Links And Images Pulled Forward To Phase 1
nodes.rationale: Owner decision, 2026-09-07: a part with a photograph and a link to where it came from is most of what makes a library worth sitting in front of, and none of it depends on anything Phase 2 onwards adds.

nodes.label: Build Graph (Blueprint Board) Spec
nodes.rationale: The largest subsystem, comparable in size to everything before it. process_type, build_graph, build_graph_revision, build_node, build_edge, build_step, build_run and build_run_node.

nodes.label: Two Graphs, Not One: BOM Tree vs Process Graph
nodes.rationale: A BOM answers what it is made of and changes with the design; a process graph answers how to make it and changes with the method. The same BOM has different process graphs for FDM versus injection moulding — exactly the hobbyist/industrial overlap — and it only works if they are separate objects. Conflating them is what makes assembly tools unusable.

nodes.label: ~15 Builtin Process Types With JSON Schema Params
nodes.rationale: Printing needs printer/material/layer height, moulding needs tool number/shot weight/cycle time/cavities. A free-text tag loses all of it; a fixed enum locks out workflows we did not predict — hence a schema per type plus user-defined types, with the palette filtered by library so a hobbyist does not scroll past injection moulding to find FDM.

nodes.label: Runs Are Instances, Graphs Are Templates
nodes.rationale: Without the split you cannot build the same assembly twice, cannot track two units in parallel, and editing a graph destroys the history of what was already built.

nodes.label: Pinned vs Floating Node Revisions
nodes.rationale: A node with revision_id null silently changes what gets built when someone uploads a new revision. Support both, show the difference clearly, default to pinned in controlled libraries and floating in hobby ones.

nodes.label: Ready-Set Ordering
nodes.rationale: Critical path first, then batch affinity (five ready parts in the same filament is one plate, not five), then shortest first so progress feels visible — that ordering is what makes it useful rather than merely correct. Quantities multiply through the graph, seeded by build_run.qty: MRP-lite, and it must stay that way. Cycles are rejected at write time via petgraph, returning which edge closed the loop, because a cycle in the database makes the ready-set query loop forever.

nodes.label: Two UIs On The Same Data: Board And Guide
nodes.rationale: The board designs the process at a desk and writes build_graph; the guide follows it on a phone at the bench and writes build_run_node. The guide is a linearization of the DAG using the ready-set ranking, but any ready step may be marked done out of order, because no real shop works strictly sequentially. Auto-generate the first draft from each process type's template: nobody writes forty steps from a blank page, and a guide that starts empty stays empty.
